"Gotovina: But now, temporarily, until we complete the task, the units need to be in contact; meaning, their commands need to be connected and that connection must be established quickly in order to be able to coordinate. In other words, the task is complete the enclosure, the pursuit of forces, taking over the line, freeing up forces for the attack, and further advancement. "DK: People are ready and we have no problem fulfilling this task. It needs to be completed as soon as possible because I support you, and we should seize this opportunity to finally complete this. Commander, I need these forces truly not to remain behind in the rear, but to have them changed so that I can go forward, because I can't hold a position and go forward. "Gotovina: That's the Sinj group, in coordination with the Sinj group. It's clear to the Sinj group what its task is and how it is supposed to cover the terrain. There is no need for all these troops in the rear which are getting lost, and I saw this passing through Vrlika, Kijevo. These are large groupings of our forces that don't need to be in this area. So now we must approach this in a planned manner; and every commander, from group commander, must get a precise order and suggest which unit needs to take over the line in order to free the 4th Guards Brigade in its breach towards Ervenik. The remaining forces of the Sibenik group will cover it in breaching to Ervenik to the point which the Sinj group covers now at this point. Is that clear to the commander of the Šibenik group? "Unknown Male: Clear. "DK: But it should already be determined commander, I mean, who shall replace me in the Strmica area. I will remain this evening so that the replacement should take place tomorrow during the day. Therefore, I have left that battalion. It is -- "Gotovina: The replacement shouldn't be conducted tomorrow but today, the troops of the Sinj group, and we have the Sibenik group who linked up, up there. What's wrong with you commanders? You don't feel like waging war anymore. You were whining there three months ago, that you needed to be kept on a leash, so that you wouldn't launch something yourselves. Now that you've got going, what's wrong with you now? Are you tired all of a sudden? "Have a meeting between the commanders of the Sinj group and the Sibenik group, assigning the troops that will replace and take over everything that the 7th Guards Brigade and the 4th Guards Brigade have been holding up to now. In this way, we free the attack forces and the Ervenik axis. Tomorrow morning, immediately, forces are to be entered for the breach of the Ervenik axis. Until then, these troops will come closer and be able to relieve the attack forces right away. "This all has to be done dynamically, the rhythm mustn't be lost, and they mustn't be allowed to now somewhere to fortify somewhere ahead of us and to resist our forces so that we suffer casualties as a result. "When the enemy is in disarray, falling apart, then you mustn't give him time to get back up on his feet, but you automatically need to push him to destruction. It's as if you had a boxer in front of you. You've dealt him a clever blow, he has fallen on his knees, and you didn't want to beat him anymore, but started jumping in the air with joy. Then he gets up and then knocks you out. "So, the commander of the Sinj group, in fact, since he's busy today with me and these others, his deputy Roko Mijic will, with the commander of the Sibenik group, assign troops, get in touch with the chief of staff of the 7th Guards Brigade, the chief of staff of the 4th Guards Brigade, elaborate a handover plan, and tomorrow morning the 4th heads out towards Ervenik. Do you understand? "DK: I'm heading out today. People are already heading out. "Gotovina: Okay. The Sinj group? "Unknown Male: I think I'll solve this by this evening. "Gotovina: Of course. The Zadar group, you got the task of coming out to Kastel Zegarski by tonight. "MF: That has already been accomplished. "Gotovina: The forces for -- in pursuit are to link up and relieve the attack forces, so we can automatically orient them on the next axis. The 7th Guards Brigade is resting. "IK: There's just one question. Where should I pull out my men? In Zivkovic's area, for further tasks? “Gotovina: Do you have a barracks -- "IK: Towards Grahovo or here in the southern barracks? There's no space down there. It is a small barracks with the larger part -- "Gotovina: Then towards Grahovo. "IK: Let's have them go to Grahovo, there where they've been, there in those houses -- "Gotovina: Go ahead. "IK: This way we set up groups and transfer -- "Gotovina: You don't need to move them because, later, that's your axis, because you're coming onto the border this way. "IK: All right. No problem. "Gotovina: Because the 4th is coming out onto the border from the left side, and the Zdrug and these others will follow in the middle. So, coordinate up there and hand over the line, you pull out to rest, and we're waiting for the next task. Okay, Romic? "All right. We'll come downstairs for cocktails. You basically all go except Kotromanovic, Filipovic, Krsticevic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, just to verify, I take it that if there's any discrepancy between the transcript as distributed and what Madam Transcriber will cut and paste, I'd like to hear it now, but I do not see there is any indication that there is a discrepancies. So, therefore, we will work on cutting and pasting. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you now have had a chance to look at the second part of the video as well, and I'd like to talk to you a little bit about the context of everything that is transpiring for General Gotovina on the 6th of August. Given that video, General Gotovina talks about 70 per cent of the task having been published by the 6th of August. Is it correct to say that the Split Military District forces, as well as other elements of the HV, still had to liberate the territory north of Knin, the Knin-Strmica area, to get to the international border of Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that on the 6th, they were not yet at the border between Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, General Gotovina there, at that point -- at that one point in the video, talks about that they had solved the issue of the military and political epicentre and, as a result, the rest came crumbing down like a house of cards. Are you familiar with the concept of -- the NATO concept of centre of gravity, and can you explain that concept and this concept of the military epicentre that General Gotovina is talking about, in the context of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. In the NATO - as a military dictionary, I'm not sure whether it is AP2 or if it has another name - but at any rate, the concept of centre of gravity is defined there as - I'm paraphrasing because I don't remember the exact definition - factors that give the opposing side his strength or his freedom of movement. This is based on what Clausewitz calls "schrerpunkt." There is a lot of philosophy and even academic articles about whether these are just like geographic concepts or whether it's about an ability or a particular type of unit. I remember, for example, one article which I think was published in Parametres, which is a American military magazine, where, for example, in the previous Gulf or in the last Iraq conflict, for example, the guards in the Iraqi armed forces were a centre of gravity. In other conflicts, a geographic concept, for example, a city or a location of a command centre can be a centre of gravity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the context of Operation Storm, would you agree that Knin was the centre of gravity for the RSK?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no doubt that Knin had an important psychological relevance or importance, both for the local Serbs as well as for the Croatian forces. But from the purely military point of view, I would, for example, also consider the corps of special units which had been recently established in the SVK as a centre of gravity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So would you say, then, that there were two centres of gravity?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... sorry.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been more. The personality of Milan Martic could have been a centre of gravity if he was the charismatic leader of the Serbs who would, if he made a move, then the other Serbs would also make a move, like, for example, we see in other conflicts. Then he could have been also defined as a centre of gravity. I haven't analysed the centre of gravity of the SVK. I'm just giving a theoretical answer based on my understanding of the term "centre of gravity" and what could have been centres of gravity within the so-called RSK and the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me just follow up on your last answer. What happens from a military or theoretical perspective, let's say, if you have said Knin was an important psychological centre and Milan Martic may have been a centre of gravity, what happens if Milan Martic is in Knin? Does that multiply the importance of both Knin and Mr. Martic? Is there a synergistic effect between the two that raises the level of the importance?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so, because it all depends of the value of Martic, on the one hand, and the value of Knin, on the on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You saw -- I hope you noted there's a portion in this video where General Gotovina yells at the commanders and says, "What's the matter with you?" I am paraphrasing now. "Have you lost your desire to fight? The last few months you've told me that I had to keep you on a leash or that you would start something yourselves." Do you recall that portion of the video?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remembered the first part of your paraphrasing here. I'm not sure whether I heard "or that would you start something yourselves." It may be possible. I am not doubting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You heard the reference to a leash?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let me call your attention to pages 319 to 320 of your report, part 2. This in the notice section that have you to General Gotovina. You write: "Ante Gotovina is familiar with the reputation and the behaviour of the subordinates during a meeting with President Tudjman and other senior HV military officials on 31 July 1995 in Brioni. Gotovina states, 'The forces heading towards Knin are 400 good infantrymen from the 3rd Battalion, the 126th Regiment, who are all from this area, and they know the area through and through. They have reason to fight here, and, at this moment, it is difficult to keep them on a leash.'" Now, correct me if I'm wrong, but was it your intention in putting that quote in the section of notice of alleged serious crimes in the zone of responsibility of the Split Military District during and after Operation Oluja, that General Gotovina's reference to keeping them on a leash was somehow intended to imply that these individuals are prone to crime, and I have to keep them on a leash?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why I put that entry there is that a commander has to be familiar with his troops, not only with the qualitative aspect, i.e., how many troop, how many tanks, but also the quantitative aspect, i.e., their combat readiness, their reputations. Some units are stronger than others. And, in particular, in this context, we know there are units made up of former refugees. Now, for a commander, that is an important signal or important indicator which may influence his decision-making process when he going to give tasks to that unit. That is one of the reasons or that is the reason why I put this excerpt of the Brioni meeting minutes in this part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But having heard General Gotovina speaking again, actually yelling back at those commanders, about "What is the matter? Have you lost your will to fight? A couple of months ago, you told me I had to keep you on a leash," do you agree with me that General Gotovina's reference there, when is he speaking at Brioni about having to keep them on a leash, refers to their battle readiness, their will to fight, their morale being high, and willingness to go into combat?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, high morale is a good thing, but one has to be very careful as a commander if morale or what looks like morale is too high, because there may well be a thin line between very high morale and desire to revenge. I emphasise this is a theoretical answer based on my training and education, and, if you want, I can give examples of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, let me try to see whether I understood your question. Was your question about using a leash as to pull the dog in the right direction; or that you use the leash in order to hold the dog back who wants to move forward too quickly. That, apparently, is the issue Mr. Misetic wants to put to you, and he, apparently, gained the impression that where you introduced it here, it was that it was difficult to keep the dog back. Whereas, he puts to you whether what he saw on the video may give a different explanation of the leash; that is, that would you have to pull the dog forward to do what -- where the dog is apparently tired, to do what it is expected to do. Mr. Misetic, that's the issue you wanted to put to Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's the second issue that I was going to address. My issue is -- actually, let me put in as simple terms as I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You make reference to the leash -- leash comment at Brioni, at page 319 and 320, in the context of the following sentences: "Ante Gotovina is familiar with the reputation and the behaviour of his subordinates." It is it in the section of notice of crime. My question to you is: He is not making reference there about "I have to keep them on a leash to hold them back from committing crime." Right? He is saying "I have to hold them back because they're so eager to get into combat and to fight the enemy that I have to hold them back on a leash." Right? That reference at Brioni has nothing to do with "These are criminals and I am having a hard time containing them."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the meeting in Brioni on 31st of July happens two or three days after the events in Bosansko Grahovo and Glamoc, which we have extensively discussed, and where there is extensive reference on looting and burning in these two cities by units of the Split Military District, and that is referred to the operational diary P71. From the document I reviewed, in particular reports by the assistant commanders for political affairs, as well as SIS and even General Lausic alludes to that, units of the Home Defence, i.e., Home Defence Regiment, are more likely or more involved to become involved in incidents of looting and burning because of their makeup. Why? They include refugees or internally displaced persons. When General Gotovina says, "who are all from this area," he indeed refers to people who have been displaced because of the conflict, and, as he describes it, they know the area through and through and they have a reason to fight. Based on my education and training and my understanding of the conflict, again, referring to the documents I have used in the report, such units, one has to be extra careful with a commander because there is a risk that they are more vulnerable to undesires or undisciplined behaviour, for example, as has been expressed in the documents reviewed in the report, looting and burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First, Mr. Theunens, let me get back to what I was focussed on. Let me first say I understand that you tend to fall back on "my experience and training," which is then impossible for me to cross-examine you on. I'm interested more in -- and you seem to do that when you can't cite to a specific document. So let us get back into the documents, okay? I'm not interested in what you would do. I'm interested in you're saying this is what General Gotovina meant in his report. All I'm trying to establish can with you is now, having seen another video where General Gotovina references earlier conversations with his subordinates - he is talking specifically about the 126th Home Guard Regiment - "What's the matter with you guys? A couple of months ago you, told me that I had to keep you on a leash, and now you are tired." Does that additional piece of information now shed some light for you about what he meant at Brioni, about keeping them on a leash?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think one important distinction is the leash obviously is the common word. But the people who are addressed in the Brioni meeting, these soldiers, subordinates, including commanders. And in the tape we have just seen, he only talks about the commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, that may be the case or may not be the case. It may be relevant, it may not be relevant. The use of the word "leash" may be indicative or insignificant. It is for the witness to tell us whether what he just saw has any effect on the conclusions, or at least the interpretation, of the quote we find on page 320, of which he explained that his interpretation was guided by both the events in, among other places, recently in Grahovo, and on the specific composition of these troops. It being that the units were composed of locals, which may have become refugees meanwhile and would return to their place of origin. That seems to be the question to me. Mr. Theunens, could you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The video I have seen does not change my conclusion. And just to be complete, I would like to refer to the quotation I make of D810, on page 339 of my report, footnote 1345.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have seen the quote and I don't know that that has to do with the leash comment, but we'll move on. There's a certain portion of the video where General Gotovina makes reference, and he says about the SIS, the military police, and political affairs, he says: "Those services protect the army during the offensive. They are the guarantee for military culture." Then he says to them: "Political affairs, SIS, and military police, you are the most responsible here." Now, can you help us understand why General Gotovina is referring to those three services as the most responsible there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not entirely sure whether the, "you are the most responsible" when General Gotovina makes that comment, refers to directly to what he stated earlier about, indeed, political affairs, SIS, and military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me read back the quote directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, could you help us. What page is it of the transcript so that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is page 4 of the transcript, third paragraph -- third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me read it for you. I don't think you have a copy of the transcript in front of you. He says: "And the guarantee for military culture and for the military reputation of an army is its political activity, security service, military police. You are the most responsible people here for all this mess that we have here. That is why we have five hours until then, fire hours to get the town itself in order, and that it be equipped with everything necessary to await the Croatian leadership. "Do you understand?" Now, help us understand why General Gotovina says that "the political activity, security service, and military police are the most responsible people here for all this mess that we have here."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In light of the documents I have reviewed, I consider this, if this is what General Gotovina said, a rather unusual conclusion, because the orders we have for the enforcement of discipline are all directed from an operational commander to his subordinate commanders. They only mention or identify SIS and political affairs as organs that can assist in achieving or in restoring discipline or preventing looting and burning. It is obvious that SIS and political affairs, they advised the commander. That's why we have an assistant commander for political affairs, an assistant commander for SIS. But these people do not have command authority. Command authority rests with the operational commander. It is up to the operational commander to use the advice he receives from his assistants for political affairs and SIS, to issue orders and, most importantly, to verify the implementation of these orders. The same applies in a different context to the military police. But SIS cannot go and talk to each an individual soldier of the military police and tell them, "Well, have you to respect discipline." That's now how it is working. It goes through the operational chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, first, while I'm looking up a document, if you could please tell me, you qualify that by saying "if that is what General Gotovina -- if this is what General Gotovina said." Is there some reason that you question the video?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't question the video. But I remember when General Gotovina makes that comment, the camera goes to the operational commanders, and I can see, for example, General Korade. Now whether that is just the way how the video is being filmed, I don't know, but that is at least based on my military background and my understanding of how such meetings go. The comment "you are responsible for this,' to me, it was clear, well, look General Gotovina has gathered his subordinate commanders for a particular reason, and this is one of the messages he wants to convey to his subordinate commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could have P918 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When we're waiting for it, Mr. Misetic, and Mr. Waespi, of course, we've seen the video or at least other portions of the video before. I don't remember exactly whether any commanders of the military police were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any agreement on who exactly is present and who is not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Also the commanders of -- there is an assistant for political affairs present from the command of the Split Military District, but there is also a "coordinator" from the political affairs branch from Zagreb who has been sent down and who is present at the meeting, and who is not a member of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, that's agreed upon about the presence of these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I have to verify whether there are more people present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I forgot to tender the second portion of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, the version we got was from the Croatian government, and I also think that what we also got is a version from the Internet, which is 65 ter 3780. I still believe that the -- what we have seen is not the complete version. So going back to my earlier point, we would like to have the complete version, if we can get it, of the whole meeting. So we would like to make sure that what we have in 3780 is encompassed by what my friend is tendering now, and we can compare that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I thought it was, Your Honour, but I could be corrected on that. I thought it did encompass what they had. I am aware of any additional material on this meeting that is in exixtance. I can tell you that the portions that I believe are deleted from the Prosecution's videos are the portions where this portion about the SIS, political affairs, and military police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently being addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was deleted from the video. Deleted from the video was General Gotovina saying "All war booty needs to be logged and collected." It was deleted from the OTP version that was provided by the Croatian government. There's one mother area, I believe, "the house of cards and the epicentre" is also not present in the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, Mr. Misetic seems to be quite confident that the portion he played was disclosed to you. Of course, if you want to compare that with other versions, even versions you may have found on the Internet, then that -- at this moment, would this cause you to object or to make a reservation, or would you say no objections, but we reserve our position, as to adding if we find more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, your last point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour this becomes Exhibit D979.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D979 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Waespi, how much time you think need to compare this so that we -- let's say within the last week at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As I said, it may very well be that there is some extra portion because, as I said, they were taken from two different cameras. So it is possible that somebody taped something a little bit before or after what I played, but I am not aware of it. I certainly would not have an objection if there was additional material that needs to be introduced. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: While we're talking about the political affairs branch and how this works, this is now Exhibit P918 which you referred to, correct, in your direct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and also in my report page 336 and 337.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let's first, if we can read the second paragraph, it is not indented, but I believe it should be a second paragraph. It says: "However ..." -- first of all, note that it is sent to assistant commanders for political affairs, meaning within the Split Military District, at all the levels in the military. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The assistant commanders for political affairs in the subordinate units. I believe on the last page, it also indicates that the Split Military District command received it for info.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is become it is coming from -- essentially from the assistant for political affairs of the Split Military District Command. Correct? It's signed on his behalf by Mr. Tomasovic, but it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we scroll to the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You see who the issuer is? It's the Split Military District who is issuing the warning.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the political affairs section. But if we go to the last page --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, no. I understand that it's copied, but let's just establish, first of all, the person sending the warning is, in fact, a member of the Split Military District Command; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'll get to the next page. The second paragraph is: "However, because of the irresponsibility of individual soldiers, non-commissioned officers, and officers, who compromise the Croatian army and state through their inappropriate conduct and acts, this success has been partly brought into question," and then there is an bolded part about the international community could undertake measures which have unforeseeable consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go to the next portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says: "For this reason and following the policy of the supreme commander, Dr. Franjo Tudjman, as well as the instructions of the defence minister and the political administration of the defence ministry of the Republic of Croatia, it is necessary to immediately prevent the following: Continued torching and destruction of facilities and property throughout the entire liberated territory; killing of livestock; confiscation of property; inappropriate conduct toward remaining civilians and prisoners of war and especially towards members and soldiers of the peace forces." Now, first, based on your review of the documents, would you agree with me, based on this document and other similar references to, for example, Mr. Lausic on the meeting in the 15th of September, who also referenced state policy and that the persons present at the meeting were the only ones responsible for complementing the policy of preventing this crime, that document, this document, would you agree with me that subordinates of President Tudjman and subordinates of Minister Susak thought that it was policy, their policy, to prevent torching and destruction of facilities, prevent killing of livestock, prevent confiscation of property, prevent inappropriate conduct toward remaining civilians, et cetera, as stated there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of the inclusion of Mr. Tudjman and Mr. Susak of the warning was intended to reinforce or to strengthen the warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I agree that that's why those are included. But based on the fact that they specifically are being included and subordinates are specifically being told that the policies of the president and the defence minister are to prevent this type of illegal conduct, do you agree with me that the subordinates of President Tudjman and Minister Susak were told that policy is to stop these things from happening?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what the document states. However, it was also stated at earlier times, and it is just an application or implementation of the Code of Discipline, that armed forces do not burn or loot or do not undertake activities as those listed in under 1, 2, 3, and 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it should be -- it's standard operating procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, the assistant for political affairs, second paragraph from the bottom, says: "In order to implement the above, political workers bear special responsibility and are required to inform the unit commanders of the above and to take measures to present crimes," and then in bold: "In cooperation with the information and security service, or SIS, and the military police, take repressive measures and launch disciplinary proceedings [sic] against those who do not abide by the instructions." Now, explain to us, especially in light of General Gotovina's comments on the video on the 6th, under the Croatian laws, rules, and regulations, how did the political affairs, SIS, and military police take repressive measures and launch disciplinary procedures in cooperation with each other?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe there's a translation issue. I have quoted from the English translation, and that's on page 337 in my report. The English translation with ERN 0306-1654 - 0306-1654, where the texts of these paragraphs is as follows: "For the implementation of this, particular responsibility shall be with the commanders of the units and political officials within the units ..." --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I can stop threw, Mr. Theunens. You obviously are unaware that both the Prosecution and the Defence are both in agreement that the translation in your report is wrong, and the translation on the screen is right. You will note that this is a P document I have put on the screen for you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not been informed of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, how does that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are by now informed that there seems to be agreement, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: We'll have to check the history of this. I'm sure that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take that we are not going to quarrel about whether there is an the agreement on an error in translation. So if would you please focus on the text as you see it on your screen at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can advise Mr. Waespi that Mr. Margetts and I both worked out that this is the accurate translation on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed. So the paragraph in the document highlights the responsibility of the members of the department for political affairs to explain the importance of the matters discussed in the warning to -- to the operational commander, in order to allow him or to encourage him to take the appropriate measures, so that the measures -- I mean, the warning is being implemented and that the unlawful activities are being stopped or prevented.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I was more -- even more interested, I should say, in the next paragraph. And if you could explain to us again with your knowledge of the rules, regulations, and laws of the Republic of Croatia, how it is that the political affairs, in cooperation with the SIS, and the military police, can take repressive measures and launch disciplinary procedures.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That paragraph is not coherent with what is stipulated in the Code of Discipline. I mean, the imposition of disciplinary measures -- I mean, the authority for the imposition of disciplinary measures lies with the operational commander. The assistant commanders for SIS and political affairs can discover crimes or violations of discipline like any other member of the armed forces, but the rest of the procedure is the operational commander, and then depending on the seriousness of the cases, the military prosecutor and military court, or military disciplinary prosecutor and military prosecutor intervene, and the military police can assist with the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I call your attention, again, to you our discussion where I pointed out, I believe, Article 15 of the regulations of the work of the military police. Do you recall that? It's about them being able to identify violators of military discipline -- disciplinary reports against violators of military discipline, bring in violators of military discipline. In other words, do you agree with me that the military police under its regulations had independent powers to monitor, identify, and bring in violators of military discipline, and file complaints against them for violations of military discipline? That is it part of their powers, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Independent but not exclusively .

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you know that, then when you read this paragraph again, where you first say that it is not coherent the Code of Discipline, isn't, in fact, very coherent? Political affairs has the duty to constantly remind, educate, and advise members of the military of their duties to comply with discipline and the law. SIS has the obligation to uncover and provide information from within the units themselves about violations of military discipline and to report on it. The military police is the executor that can then take action against those violators once that information is received, bring them in, and have a disciplinary report filed against the individual. Aren't all three services, in fact, compatible in what their functions are in enforcing discipline?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, they can play a role, but it -- the Code of Discipline does not state, for example, that the assistant commander for SIS can impose disciplinary measures. It is the operational commander. It is also the operational commander from the company commander level onwards who can arrest alleged perpetrators. There is no mention in the Code of Discipline that such an authority or such a power lies with the assistant commander for political affairs or the assistant commander for SIS. I think I would also like to draw your attention to 65 ter 2305, which is addressed in on pages 335 and 336 of my report. And if you allow me, I will read out one of the paragraphs I have quoted in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have a feeling I know where we're going. First of all, I think you have covered that in your direct. So let's -- in the interests of time, let's focus again, because you then, in your answer, limit yourself to SIS and political affairs not being able to take specific measures. That's not what I said in my question. You left out the military police part. Now, the military police, in fact, can take measures, file reports for violations of discipline, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I answered you that question where I said it is not exclusively the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. No one said it was exclusively military police. But in terms of the scheme, when General Gotovina on the 6th is telling them, "You are the people most responsible," among their jobs is to bring to the attention of commanders violations of discipline. For example, at check-points, if there are soldiers who are caught with looted goods, right, somebody from the military police has to file a disciplinary report with that person's commander saying, "This person was caught at a check-point with stolen goods." Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, indeed, among the jobs of the military police to inform the operational commander of such activities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if, for example, a commander finds that 150 of his men have not reported for duty, on a particular day or in a particular week, their roaming liberated territories, he doesn't know where they are, whose job is it to find them and bring them back? So they -- for example, if they are engaging in crime, they can come back to the unit and appropriate measures can be taken against them.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. I think, in that context, it is important to draw your attention to Article 25 of P880, where it is stated that commanders of brigades, independent battalions, equal and higher HV commanders, are authorised to send such requests to the military police battalion. So the start of the search activity or the initiative, I'm sorry, is taken by the operational commander, and that is the whole issue we are discussing here. Obviously, it is clear that the military police has a task to perform, and there are some aspects they perform on their. But it is -- the operation commander cannot say, well, it is not my problem, it is the military police. No. He has a responsibility to enforce discipline in his units, and he can use the military police as a tool, and, therefore, he can give instructions to the military police to assist him. That is how it functions in the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Of course. Now you are arguing something that General Gotovina never says in the video. He says "You are the most responsible." He doesn't say, "You are solely responsible."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was trying to answer to your question, because you had a particular question about 150 soldiers roaming. Indeed, the military police can then be used in order to locate these individuals and bring them to the unit. But the order or the -- I mean, it is the operational commander who issues the initial task to the military police or who requests them to locate and bring in these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In that that context. In a different context, for example, at check-point, it is up to the military police itself to report that. They don't need a specific request from a commander to say, "Tell me how many of my men you caught at check-point looting." Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They will inform the operational commander if they catch or they discover members of his unit who are involved in illegal activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Theunens, I'd like to go back to the Knin video for one moment. You noticed that there that General Gotovina gives an oral order about the logging of war booty. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are also written orders from General Gotovina to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Let me -- while we're on the topic of what is happening on 6th and 7th, let me also show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I please have 1D63-0195.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: These are -- what I am about to show you, Mr. Theunens, I don't believe you have seen before. We have translated an excerpt from the minutes of the 259th Session of the Government of the Republic of Croatia held on the 7th of August, 1995. You see, at the top, what these are the minutes of. You can see all -- the prime minister is present, the various deputy prime ministers, the various ministers including Ministers Susak and Jarnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 in the English translation, please, which is page 3 of the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's Minister of Defence Susak reporting to the government. He states: "The operation was completed quicker than was expected for which credit must also be given to the excellent cooperation between the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Interior which immediately set up police station within the liberated areas. The Minister of Defence Susak also stated that he had signed a decision for the demobilisation of 70.000 soldiers today. And on page 4 of the Croatian. It says: "The minister of the interior, Ivan Jarnjak, informed the government that the Croatian police had assumed the task of ensuring public order and peace within the newly liberated territories, adding that the members of the civilian protection services were entering these territories to conduct the sanitation of the terrain. "The minister of the internal affairs also thanked the minister of defence for the exceptional cooperation between the two ministries during this operation." Now, Mr. Theunens, when were you were preparing your report, were you aware that, as of, at the latest, the 7th of August, the Ministry of Internal Affairs had taken over in the newly liberated territories the task of ensuring public order and peace?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of -- I was not aware of the specific date, but I am familiar with the fact that civilian police stations are being established, including for the purpose of ensuring public order and -- and the rule of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I asked that this exhibit be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D980.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D980 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could please have 65 ter 982, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is an order following the meeting on the 6th. General Gotovina issues another order which says: "With reference to the indicated need to register the war booty on the liberated territory, I here issue the following order ..." And he forms a committee: "A committee shall be formed at the Split Military District level for registering and recording complete war booty on the liberated territory in the Split Military District zone of responsibility, and the committee shall consist of the following members." The members of the committee are identified. "The tasks of the committee are to register and record the war booty in the Split Military District zone. Distribution of weapons, ammunition, and explosives. If we could turn to page 3, item 7. He orders that: "The committee chairman shall submit a comprehensive written report by 1800 hours on 11 August 1995." Now, looking at this order and combined with what General Gotovina says at the meeting on the 6th, he is taking measures actually to verify what his subordinate units are registering as war booty. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And this document is also included in my report on page 376, part 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this exhibit be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D981, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D981 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Misetic, any way of perhaps hearing from this witness what the TTS abbreviation stands for?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you tell us the committees tasks shall be as follows, and then the second, distribution of weapons, ammunition, and explosives, and TTS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to check, Mr. President. But if I'm allowed during the break, I can ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you -- at any later point in time you could assist us, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: MTS stands for military technical goods, so that's twice, the S, but I will check for the T, TS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. President, let me just note that I have, rather than take time here, I have several reports from subordinate units listing their war booty which I will prepare a chart and give it to the Prosecution and move from the bar table about all the reports of the subordinate units on what war booty they reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I have seen the documents. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm -- may I take it that you will prepare a list for Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think bar table documents, wasn't there a procedure which we -- so that we know also what we're talking about. I think I -- the Chamber give instructions that it should be clear what to focus on. Sometimes they are more lengthy; documents sometimes -- perhaps you would just a brief description to be given to the other party to see whether there's any objection against characterizing the document or the specific portion which we are supposed to pay attention to so that we are not just guided by numbers but also by the characterization of content which assists us in deciding on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will certainly no later than Monday do that, and I will put it on the record as to what exactly it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens -- let me find one document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One moment, please. Mr. Registrar, if I could 65 ter 2305, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe you made reference to this report on direct examination as well. Now, this is another report from the political activities unit for OG North. In it, it's reported that Colonel Ivan Zelic and Colonel Ivan Ceko, pursuant to an order of Lieutenant-General Ante Gotovina, if we could scroll down a little bit, concerning performing the assignments relating to political activities and providing support to the civilian structures and overseeing all other elements transferred on to Knin, 5 August 1995, in order it carry out the assignments there. The legal assistant paragraph says: "Moreover, due to inertia and lack of readiness on the part of civilian bodies and structures to carry out their tasks immediately in the first days and to take on further organisation and management of the town, we have encountered a lot of problems that were impossible to solve without the support of civilian bodies, and there are attempts to put the blame for this on the PD service." Now, as part of your analysis of events here, is it correct that part of the problems in restoring order in the newly liberated territories generally and Knin specifically was the lack of preparedness by the civilian structures to establish law and order quickly upon liberation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn the page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do wish me to answer now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. The problem in relation with the civilian authorities is, based on the documents I reviewed, is a problem to -- to be effective, i.e., their ability to restore order and law, and it's not so much a question of preparedness or readiness. The documents I see indicate, like, they try but they can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was that a general problem? Both civilian and military structures, they're trying but they can't?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I -- I mean, my answer in the previous question refers to, for example, the letters Mr. Moric, assistant minister of the interior, sends to General Lausic. There are several ones during the second half of the month of August, where Mr. Moric complains or states that the civilian police cannot act against people in uniform and cannot establish whether they are really military or not. Now, that the military structures are trying but can't, I mean, then we have a fundamental problem with the military, because, as we have seen, military discipline is one of the duties of the commander. If he cannot enforce or restore discipline among his units, then he -- he should inform his superiors of that, and instead of conducting combat operations where actually a high level of discipline is essential to be successful, and that was also pointed out by, I think, General Gotovina at the video, he should inform his superior commander about the problems he has and request the superior commander to postpone the launching of combat operations until he, i.e., the subordinate commander, has managed to restore discipline among his units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, in light of the fact that you have seen numerous orders being issued, again, my question was: Do you agree that the will was there. In certain cases the execution failed on both the civilian and military sides in the early days of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have only systematically removed military documents and the conclusion I have drawn, in relation to the enforcement of discipline only addresses -- is only based on these military documents, whereby my conclusion is that the rate -- I mean, the volume of orders and the rate at which they are issued by the Split Military District as well as by subordinate commanders, indicated there is a problem with the implementation or the enforcement of these orders. If you have to issue an order for specific activity or to stop active several times, well, things will not get better by just re-issuing the orders. You have to as a commander envisage other measures, first of all, verify why you have -- why the order you have issued is not abided by, and then subsequently change your approach, and maybe undertake additional measures, in order to guarantee that the orders you issue are implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Rest assured, Mr. Theunens, you and I will be discussing that topic and that opinion shortly. However, is the answer to the question I posed "Yes"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the conclusion for the military is, indeed, that the execution, based on documents I reviewed, failed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But the will was there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I tried to understand what the answer of the witness to your question is. You tried to simplify matters. I understand the answer of the witness to be that, on the basis of the orders issued, that that expresses a will and, at the same time, he draws our attention to the fact that if these orders are not implemented, that he would expect something in addition or something else to be done, in order to make that will effective on the ground. So whether it is yes or no, I think that the answer is a bit more complex. Have you understood your answer well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: As I said, Mr. President, with regard to that second opinion, you'll hear a lot in cross-examination soon on that opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm just trying to understand. You more or less saying to the witness, Now was it yes or no? He gave an answer with more shades of grey than you put to him when you ask him, Is it black and white. That's what I what I wanted to clarify. Mr. Misetic, you said that you would go over several matters with the witness, but I take it that will you do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break, and we will resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have Exhibit D204, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is, Mr. Theunens, as you know, the order of General Gotovina on 10th of August. In it, he says he is basing this information from the areas liberated by the HV. I'll just note that one of those pieces of information would be that report from the 6th Home Guards commander, Mr. Klarec, that you used on direct, I believe, the day before. And following that, he issues another order which is to prevent theft of property, undisciplined conduct, and to save human lives. The first point is: "I prohibit arbitrary movement of the HV members in the liberated areas without the knowledge of their superior commanders." Now the fact that that is point 1 of the order, does that, from a military point of view, indicate that that is a problem that he is trying to resolve?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that General Gotovina includes this instruction in his order, indeed, means from the military point of view that there have been problems in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which would mean problems in the fact that the soldiers were arbitrarily moving in the liberated areas without the knowledge of their superior commanders. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll down please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He then orders that they: "Take all necessary measures and fully engage in the implementation of the military disciplinary conduct and the maintenance of order in the area of responsibility and prevent arson and all other illegal acts. Take resolute measures against anybody who conducts himself in an undisciplined manner."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The order entered into force immediately, and I designate the commanders of the directly subordinated units to be in charge of its implementation." Now, I don't know if you want me to if through, but you will agree with me that these orders were then passed down to subordinate commanders. We have examples as D841, D644, D205, as examples. Those are, for example, the order, D644, is the commander of the 142nd passing it down. D205 is the commander of the 113th passing it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could have on the screen --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I just say something about this document here, D204. I think it is also important to note that it is sent to the command of OG Zadar, which actually links it to the events that happened in Benkovac after it was -- or control was taken over Benkovac by units of the Split Military District. We have 65 ter 2741 on page 328 of part two of my report that provides additional background.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you don't know whether 65 ter 2741 was the foundation for this order or not, other than the fact that Benkovac falls within operative group Zadar; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the fact that in Benkovac, there were problems after the entry of units of the Split Military District in relation to the matters highlighted in General Gotovina's order. And 65 ter 2741 describes these problems in great detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that you giving a partial explanation there, because that is on the 5th. Then on the 6th and 7th and 8th, it talks about problems because civilians are entering Benkovac and causing problems; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. But I think at the introduction of the question, you refer to a particular document, and I thought it was useful also to draw the Trial Chamber's attention to other documents dealing with the same issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right. And let me just invite you, if you can, to try to stick to the questions, because we tend to have to go off on a tangent when you insist on finding things useful to insert into your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I please have D841 on the screen, please. Mr. President, I'm reminded that before the break, I showed 65 ter 2305 and failed to ask that it be marked and tendered. I don't know if the Prosecution has already tendered it. It may be on their list already.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I have to check that, but obviously I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Misetic that was the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 10th of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 10th August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Reporting on the failure of the civilian structures on the 5th of August to carry out assignments there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Waespi. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D982.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D982 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is now the OG Sibenik order passing down General Gotovina's order. It is issued on the same day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So, just so that we follow how things are transpiring, on the 10th of August, General Gotovina issues another order, subordinate commanders pass that order down. Before the break, we saw the political affairs warning from the 13th of August that was issued by the political affairs assistant from the Split Military District to political affairs workers, and that is within a period of about three days. Now, I'd like to talk to you a little bit about what is happening militarily in the zone of responsibility of the Split Military District between the 11th of August and, let's say, the 19th of August. Is there any combat going on that the Split Military District is engaged during that week?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I discussed those aspects on English page 146 of part 2 of the report, where I stated main tasks initially consist of mopping-up the area, i.e., remove or eliminate remaining enemy presence. On the 12th of August, and that is based on P482, the VRS carries out a limited counter-attack in the Bosansko Grahovo area. General Gotovina reacts by ordering a counter-attack by battalions belonging to the 4th and 7th Guards Brigade. That, again, comes from P428, as well as 65 ter 1128. There is an order on the 13th of August by the 7th Home Guard Regiment for mopping-up operations. Based on the military system, I mean, command and control, the order should have come from the superior command of the 7th Home Guard Regiment, and again then from the superior command of that command and that would be the command of the Split Military District. I don't know whether you want me to continue through the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a different question, and you've pointed out to the right topic. How many casualties did the HV take during that week?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have seen casualties figures in documents, but I have no exact recollection of particular figures for that week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could please have 65 ter 1200, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the weekly report of the Split Military District to the Main Staff for the week of 11 August to 18 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we scroll down the first page, it talks about enemy offensive activities in OG Vrba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Enemy was actively using its artillery, multiple rocket launchers and, tanks against the defence front line, as well as in depth of the territory on August 1995. "OG Sajkovic, on August 13th 1995, the enemy was active in the area of the Derala mountain pass using its artillery and infantry. At around 0630 hours, the enemy managed to breakthrough the front defence line taking the positions at Biljeg, Cigelj, Vidovica ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we turn the page, please. 2.1: "Measures taken: On August 13, units of OG Sajkovic area of responsibility were busy in recapturing lost positions and in organising a counter-attack permanently securing the Derala pass." Again, at the next point, on the 14th, they launched an offensive to recapture lost positions. 15th, there's more units attack in the direction of Bosansko Grahovo and Resanovci. Go to the bottom, which is section 2.3: "Our losses in the reporting period."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we turn the page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "On August 13, 1995, 14 members of the 141st HV Brigade and one member of the 6th Home Guard Regiment were killed, two seriously wounded, and 72 were lightly wounded or injured as a result of the enemy's combat activities along the direction Drvar, Grahovo, Derala Pass, Knin. On 15th August, during the HV units' offensive in the direction of Drvar, two members of the 126th Home Guard Regiment were killed, two members of the 4th HV guards were seriously wounded; whereas, three members of the 4th Guards Brigade, and two members of the 113th Infantry Brigade were lightly wounded." Now, from a military perspective, Mr. Theunens, taking 15 casualties in a three-day period is a significant event, is it not? I mean 15 deaths, especially for the Split Military District?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, and the commander would be taking appropriate action as to have an investigation mounted in order to determine the causes of this high losses, and then, obviously, take measures to avoid a reputation of such high losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, these high losses, does that indicate to you that there was serious counter-offensive by the Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, because it could, for example, be that these soldiers were caught by surprise, that they were not alert. It could be that they were, for example, on the front line in an unprotected position, there's an impact of an artillery -- of artillery grenades. They haven't been warned in time to go to their fortified positions, and then you would have such high losses. So I think the matter is more complicated than just say, well, 15 people killed, so there has to be a severe attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's look at P1131, Mr. Registrar, if you would, please. 1131.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a document you used in direct examination, and this is an order signed by General Ademi on General Gotovina's behalf. It says: "In accordance with the need and in order to secure tactical in-depth defence, for the remaining or inserted groups of enemy soldiers, I hereby order: "The commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion shall urgently send an anti-terrorist platoon to the area of Strmica with a task to search and mop-up the general area of Strmica for the remaining or inserted enemy groups. "2, The search of the terrain is to be carried out together with the parts of the 6th Home Guard Regiment deployed in the area of Strmica. "3, Details of the task will be given to the ATG commander upon reporting to the Split Military District Command, Knin IZM in Knin. "4, Deadline for the execution of this order is immediately." Now, you have talked several times about documents not being taken out of context. The context of this order is that the Split Military District Command has taken 14 casualties killed on that day; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is it part of the context, yes. These events seem to happen on the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, from a military perspective, do you see given the close prosecution its of Strmica to the Bosansko Grahovo area and the fact that these deaths occur in the area of Bosnia, why a commander would want to send to an anti-terrorist in his depth behind him to search and mop-up the terrain for remaining and inserted enemy groups, given that he has taken 14 deaths on that day?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the commander will have made his what he would call appreciation. Taking into the account the nature of the terrain and the nature of the enemy he expects there, he is uses what he considers the most appropriate force or unit or type of unit he has available, and that's why, among his forces, he uses the anti-terrorist group of the 72nd Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when we were talking about when an operational commander uses the military police, is this an example of an operational commander in the military District employing the military police for a combat purpose, to assist his responsibilities as an operational commander?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This order to mop-up was not, would you agree, as part of a mop-up order generally after Operation Storm related to leftover RSK units, necessarily?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, strictly speaking, the document does not allow to conclude to which army, whether it is SVK or VRS, these remaining groups belong. However, in context of the previous document, yes, that would point towards VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Mr. Theunens, I'd like to go back to P71 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: English page 109; B/C/S page 69. I again failed to tender 65 ter 1200, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D983, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D983 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Go to the entry on the right-hand side of the screen, and on the right-hand side in the Croatian as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is an entry again you referenced in direct examination. It concerns General Gotovina's reference to where it says "preparations for the winter" in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we go to page, let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Maybe you can help me, Mr. Theunens. I'm looking for the entry "they will winter in houses that were burned."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the entry, but, unfortunately, I didn't bring hard copies with me. But I can check also in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page in the English, please, and one more time. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I specifically mentioned the entry about spending winter in burnt out houses in my report, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think it I found it on page 359 in Mr. Theunens's report: "On 16th August 1995, General Gotovina, during the daily meeting with his subordinate commanders ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says, "the houses that are burning down. "They will stay during winter in the houses they are burning down." Now, given the context of what had transpired in the three days prior as to where the HV unit were engaged in combat, the reference there as to where these houses are, in terms of the burning, is in Bosnia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think -- I don't think that this entry allows to draw any conclusions on that aspect, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you how I interpret it. If he is talking about houses in the Republic of Croatia, these units are not -- there is no front line in Croatia where they would have to be barracked in houses somewhere in the territory the Republic of Croatia on the 16th of August. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't think we can draw such a conclusion, because it may well be there is a lack of barracks or suitable barracks that have been already been secured, in a sense that, even if the SVK have left there, the barracks they occupied, there is a need to check whether these barracks are safe, and then it is a whole logistical exercise to reoccupy them. I`m not in a position to say whether the existing barracks or other buildings in the zone of the Split Military District on Croatian territory were sufficient to house all the units of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then, is it safe to say you're not aware whether he is referring to burning going on in Bosnia or burning going on in Croatia, based on that answer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I please have 1D63-0118, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's talk a little bit about what was transpiring on the 18th of August. This is a SIS report that I'm going to show you, dated 18 August 1995. You can see at the -- in middle of the first page, it says: "Pursuant to orders, the Operative Group West is comprised of the following units," and it identifies them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, it says: "The following security problem versus been observed in OG West. Second bullet point paragraph there: "According to the operational information gathered so far, the situation is the worst in the 134th Home Guard Regiment, and it can be observed in the following: The line of command within the unit is not functioning, the commander lacks the necessary authority to implement orders issued by OG West, members of the unit are continuously destroying and burning residential buildings within the area of responsibility." Skipping a paragraph: "Members of the SIS gave out warnings that in the course of carrying out combat activities, the OG West was in command, which resulted in the removal of," and then it is blacked out, unit member, (currently carrying out the duty of assistant commander for SIS in the Benkovac garrison), and a reserve member of the SIS from the 3rd Battalion of the 134th Home Guards by battalion commander Zeljko Usljebrk." Next bullet point: "Upon arriving in the area of responsibility of OG West, we observed that the same was not secured by MP control check-points, which resulted in a large number of the members of the units within the AOR having personal vehicles and the previously mentioned incidents with the Belgian TV news team. "On the basis of our proposal dated 19 August 1995 at 0800 hours, a military police check-point shall be set up on the Knin HV Gracac Srb cross roads." Now, on 18 August, information is given --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, let me just clarify, and I think it is clarified in Mr. Theunens's report, but the OG names were changed after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There is clearly a problem in the 134th Home Guard Regiment. The commander unable to carry out orders which you mentioned as one of the problems as implementation of orders. So let's take it through now what happened in the 134th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we go to P1143, please. Mr. President, I ask that the exhibit be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections. What is the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 18 August. I believe the reference to the check-point being set up on the 19th is saying that it "shall be," meaning that this is a future event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D984.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D984 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You have an order that you used in direct examination, Mr. Theunens, which General Ademi first orders that that check-point that's referenced in the SIS report be set up?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At point 1: "That the check-point shall be put into operation on 19th of August. Only motor vehicles with a regular vehicle log shoot are to be allowed through, while the entry of civilian motor vehicles into the zone is strictly forbidden. "Allow war booty to be taken out only if there are proper lists signed by the commanders of units."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go to the next document, which is again back to P71, please, English page 115 -- actually, Mr. Registrar, I apologise. Let me show him a different document first. My apologies. Mr. Registrar, if could I please have 65 ter 860, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
