utterances.text: Following this report of the commander of the 134th being unable to implement orders and their problems, in addition to the military police check-point, an order is issued again, signed for General Gotovina: "Have a commission carry out a check. Enlist the war booty of the 134th Home Guard Regiment. For the implementation of this task, I am assigning a commission made up of following members." The members of the commission are identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The basic task of the commission is to compare what was recorded on the ground with what was listed as war booty by the unit. "Submit a written report following completion of the task. The deadline for implementation is immediately." Mr. Theunens, would you agree with me that on the basis of the information on the 18th, that a commission is formed then to conduct an inspection of the 134th to see whether the war booty they have physically matches the war booty they have identified on their lists?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we can conclude from this two documents -- from these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this exhibit be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this becomes Exhibit D985.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D985 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have Exhibit D650, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is an order issued the next day by the commander of Operative Group West: "Due do to the observed break down of order and discipline and for the international reputation for the Republic of Croatia, I hereby order ..." Then: "Establish control in all units ... take measures against the torching of buildings and killing of animals ... take disciplinary and criminal measures against irresponsibility individuals. "The commanders of OG West units are responsible to me for the implementation of this order."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could scroll to the bottom please, of the Croatian, so I can see the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, it's Colonel Fuzul.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit D884, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says -- and I will show you if necessary through a document that is issued subsequent to this and pursuant to this order that this order is issued on or about the 18th of August as well or the 19th of August. It says: "Based on the oral order by the Deputy Commander of the Split Military District, staff Brigadier Ademi, with the purpose of improving the control and reinforcing the discipline in the Split Military District units, all commanders of units in the zone of responsibility of Operative Group West can according to their own judgement dismiss part of the soldiers from their units, principally dismiss individuals or groups who are behaving in a manner that causes disturbance of discipline and order?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I expected to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will give you a question after we've rune through the documents.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is actually a key issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Make a little note what the key issue. Let's wait until Mr. Misetic has finished. And if you consider it in view of the question he will put to you still a key issue, include it in your answer. If you consider it a key issue outside his question, then please tell us at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit D885, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There is now an order passed down to the commander of the 134th. It says: "A part of the conscripts may be dismissed from the unit. "Primarily dismiss the individuals and groups who, with their behaviour, disturb the order and discipline within the unit and, as such, significantly impair the implementation of combat tasks." Now, I'm sorry I'm rushing through this, but I would like to finish this line of questioning before we end for the day. I'd like to show you a document that we will be referring to. This is the result of the inspection conducted by the Main Staff of the Split Military District completed on the 30th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, it is 65 ter 1335, please. If we could first turn to page 5 in the English, please, which is numbered page 3 in the Croatian. So two pages back in the Croatian. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any possibility to show the English on the screen as well?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is possible that the English translation hasn't been released in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I do have it in e-court if I open 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But to release it is a special activity needed to give it via the distribution. Perhaps we could use the time when waiting. Mr. Theunens, earlier you said there was a key issue. If that key issue would be that dismissing active duty men rather than to investigate disciplinarily or in a criminal context, the Chamber is not unfamiliar and has heard quite some evidence on that issue, whether what would be the most appropriate way to react and whether it would be, as a matter of fact, a heavier penalty to send people home rather than to investigate them and/or cut 10 percent of their salary, for example. So the Chamber is not unfamiliar with that aspect, if that is what was on your mind. I'm not opening any discussion on it, just filling in the time when we are still waiting for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is just an additional aspect. That is, that my understanding of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. I just wanted to let you know that at least this is a matter the Chamber has some familiarity with and not to say that in full detail. And then I would like to -- even to Mr. Misetic, but in later answering the question or further commenting, you have at least some information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I propose that we show the English translation via Sanction for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's look at it through Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, one of the findings is, if you look at "planned inspections."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks as if is now on -- yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Planned inspections and controls have not been fully established in the liberated areas yet but considerable progress has been achieved in the prevention of theft, destruction of houses and similar, which should continue to be considered a priority and permanent task." And then if I could call your attention specifically to what happened to the 134th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 37, please, to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In reporting on the inspection of the 134th: "By the order of the defence minister based on the proposal submitted by the operative group and the order of the Split Military District, the approved numerical strength of the regiment was 581 soldiers. After the demobilization, the number fell to 579. The regiment's structure was adapted accordingly. "According to the commander's order, there were -- the regiment sent 392 members on leave. The 187 members who remain in the units are engaged on the clearing of warehouses and facilities, sorting the war booty, carrying out the engineering inspections ..." Next paragraph is: "The regiment command is not brought up to establishment in accordance with the establishment plans ..." Now this regiment typically has how many people?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the earlier entry said something like -- if we go to the bottom of page 37. Stop. The numerical -- or the approved numerical strength was 581, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But how much was it at the time of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look in my report. I don't know by heart, but I have a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from having a document, I would say that you've got 72 hours to look at the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should be faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is even 72 and a half hour because we'll adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May I at least have this exhibit marked and tender it into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It is a fairly long, but I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If is fairly long. If a further redaction of the size -- I'm not saying that it can be achieved but would you at least consider it, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without of course loosing context. Mr. Theunens, I'd like to instruct you as I did all these days, that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony, whether given already or still to be given. We'd like to see you back Monday, in the afternoon. We adjourn, and we resume at Monday, the 1st of December, quarter part 2.00 in the afternoon, in this same courtroom I.
